rot.doubleAttack.ideia.ex1.e1: Attack: the knight fork is one case of a double attack, a move in which one piece attacks two targets at the same time. The queen, the rook and the bishop make their own, from a distance.
rot.doubleAttack.ideia.ex1.e2: This position comes from a game played on Lichess. Black is ahead in material, but the king is on g7, and the rook on e7 has no defender.
rot.doubleAttack.ideia.ex1.p: Find the queen move that gives check and attacks the rook on e7.
rot.doubleAttack.ideia.ex1.certo: Yes: the queen captures the pawn on f6 with check to the king on g7 and, from the same square, attacks the rook on e7. The rook on f1 defends the queen.
rot.doubleAttack.ideia.ex1.revela: The move is to capture the pawn on f6: from there the queen checks the king on g7 and attacks the rook on e7. The rook on f1 defends the queen.
rot.doubleAttack.ideia.ex1.err.f4d4.1: The queen captures the knight on d4 and wins back the piece, but without check and with only one target.
rot.doubleAttack.ideia.ex1.err.f4d4.2: With this move Black has a resource: the rook leaves e7 for f7 and defends the pawn on f6.
rot.doubleAttack.ideia.ex1.err.f4d4.3: Back to the position: look for the queen move that attacks the king and the rook.
rot.doubleAttack.ideia.ex1.fora: That move does not attack the king and the rook at once. Look for a square within the queen's reach that touches both.
rot.doubleAttack.ideia.ex1.volta: Try again: look for the queen move.
rot.doubleAttack.ideia.ex1.l1: With the check, Black must deal with the king first, and the rook on e7 has no time to escape.
rot.doubleAttack.ideia.ex1.l2: The king cannot capture the queen, defended by the rook on f1, so it steps out of check to g8.
rot.doubleAttack.ideia.ex1.l3: The queen captures the rook on e7, and White wins the material back.
rot.doubleAttack.ideia.ex1.l4: In positions like this, with the king on one side and an undefended piece on the other, the double attack with check is the strongest: the opponent has no time to save the piece.
rot.doubleAttack.ideia.ex2.e1: Attack: now a double attack without check. Both black rooks, on a8 and on f3, are undefended.
rot.doubleAttack.ideia.ex2.p: Find the square from which the bishop attacks both rooks.
rot.doubleAttack.ideia.ex2.certo: Yes: on d5 the bishop attacks the rook on a8 and the rook on f3, one on each diagonal, and no black piece attacks d5.
rot.doubleAttack.ideia.ex2.revela: The square is d5: from there the bishop attacks both rooks, and no black piece attacks the bishop.
rot.doubleAttack.ideia.ex2.err.e6g4.1: On g4 the bishop attacks the rook on f3, but only that one.
rot.doubleAttack.ideia.ex2.err.e6g4.2: With this move Black has a resource: the rook leaves f3 for f4 and attacks the bishop as well.
rot.doubleAttack.ideia.ex2.err.e6g4.3: Back to the position: look for the bishop square that reaches both rooks.
rot.doubleAttack.ideia.ex2.fora: That move does not attack both rooks at once. Look for the bishop square that reaches a8 and f3.
rot.doubleAttack.ideia.ex2.volta: Try again: look for the bishop square.
rot.doubleAttack.ideia.ex2.l1: Without check, Black has one move to answer. The best defence is to pull the rook on f3 back to f8, where it defends the one on a8.
rot.doubleAttack.ideia.ex2.l2: The rook retreats to f8. Even defended, the rook on a8 is still attacked.
rot.doubleAttack.ideia.ex2.l3: The bishop captures the rook on a8.
rot.doubleAttack.ideia.ex2.l4: The rook recaptures, but White has traded the bishop for a rook. In positions like this, with two undefended pieces within reach of the same square, the double attack wins material even without check.
rot.doubleAttack.demos.torre.1: Attack: now the rook. The black king on f7 and the undefended black knight on f5 stand on the same file. See whether the rook on d6 reaches both.
rot.doubleAttack.demos.torre.2: The rook goes to f6: it checks the king on f7 and, along the same file, attacks the knight on f5. The pawn on g5 defends the rook.
rot.doubleAttack.demos.torre.3: The king cannot capture the rook, defended by the pawn, so it steps out of check to g7. The knight is still attacked.
rot.doubleAttack.demos.torre.4: The rook captures the knight on f5.
rot.doubleAttack.demos.dama.1: Attack: now let us think from Black's side. The white king is on g1, and the white rook on a3 is undefended.
rot.doubleAttack.demos.dama.2: The queen goes to c1: it checks the king along the first rank and, along the diagonal, attacks the rook on a3.
rot.doubleAttack.demos.dama.3: The king steps out of check to g2, and the rook is still attacked.
rot.doubleAttack.demos.dama.4: The queen captures the rook on a3.
rot.doubleAttack.demos.excecao.1: Attack: Black again. The knight on d6 attacks the rook on c8. The black rook and the black queen each have a double attack. Which of them works?
rot.doubleAttack.demos.excecao.2: The rook goes to c2 and attacks the queen on e2 and the bishop on b2. It looks like a double attack.
rot.doubleAttack.demos.excecao.3: But c2 is not a safe square: the queen on e2 reaches it and captures the rook. Here the double attack just gives up the rook.
rot.doubleAttack.demos.excecao.4: Back to the position: before a double attack, check whether the arrival square is safe. If an enemy piece captures for free, both attacks vanish.
rot.doubleAttack.demos.excecao.5: If the square has one of your defenders and only a more valuable piece can reach it, as with the defended knight fork, capturing costs the opponent material, and the double attack still works.
rot.doubleAttack.demos.excecao.6: On b6 no white piece reaches the queen: it checks the king on g1 along the diagonal and attacks the knight on d6 along the rank.
rot.doubleAttack.demos.excecao.7: The king steps out of check to h1, and the knight on d6 is still attacked.
rot.doubleAttack.demos.excecao.8: The queen captures the knight on d6, the piece that was attacking the rook on c8.
rot.doubleAttack.pratica.valeAqui.enunci: Stay with Black. The queen on b5 can go to e2, with check and an attack on the bishop on d2. Does the double attack work here? Check whether the square is safe and play as Black.
rot.doubleAttack.pratica.valeAqui.fim: On e2 the king would capture the queen. On d3 the knight, defended by the queen on b5, gave check and attacked the rook on c1; the white queen took it and was taken.
rot.doubleAttack.pratica.valeAqui.err.b5: With the check on e2 you give up the queen: no black piece defends e2, and the white king captures it.
rot.doubleAttack.pratica.valeAqui.err.b4: On a2 the knight attacks the rook on c1, but without check: White has time to save the rook. Look for a move with check.
On c2 the knight gives check, but the rook on c1 captures it. Look for a check on a square your queen defends.
rot.doubleAttack.pratica.bispo.enunciado: Back to White. The black king is on g7, and the black rook on b2 is undefended. Play as White and find the best move.
rot.doubleAttack.pratica.bispo.fim: On e5 the bishop checked the king on g7 and, along the same diagonal, attacked the rook on b2: the king stepped out of check, and the bishop captured the rook.
rot.doubleAttack.pratica.bispo.err.c5c6: The pawn advances, but it attacks no piece, and Black gains time. Look for a check that also attacks the rook on b2.
rot.doubleAttack.pratica.bispo.err.d6a6: The rook captures a pawn, but there is a move that wins the rook on b2. Look for a check that also attacks it.
rot.doubleAttack.pratica.bispo.err.f4h6: The bishop captures the pawn on h6 with check, but from h6 it does not reach the rook on b2: the king steps out of check, and the rook is safe. Look for a check that also attacks the rook.
rot.doubleAttack.pratica.semXeque.enunci: Stay with White. The black bishops, on d5 and on d2, are undefended. Play as White and find the best move.
rot.doubleAttack.pratica.semXeque.fim: On d4 the rook attacked both bishops along the file, without check. With one move Black saved only one bishop, and the rook captured the other with check.
rot.doubleAttack.pratica.semXeque.err.c4: The rook attacks the bishop on d2, but only that one: the bishop escapes and even captures the pawn on f4. Look for the square that attacks both bishops.
The rook leaves the fourth rank and attacks no bishop: the bishop on d2 captures the pawn on f4. Look for the square that attacks both bishops.
